summary: Defines a BGP-4 optional parameter called Capabilities, which lets two peers advertise supported features without having to tear down the peering when new features come. It is on the standards track and was replaced by RFC 3392.

eli5.summary: Two routers say hello and tell each other what extra tricks they know. If one does not know a trick, they skip it and keep working.

questions: how do bgp peers negotiate features
what is bgp optional parameter type 2
what is bgp unsupported capability error
subtitle: A BGP OPEN option that lets peers announce optional features without dropping the session.

tldr.problem: BGP-4 required a speaker to terminate peering when an OPEN message carried an unrecognized Optional Parameter, which made new BGP features hard to introduce.
tldr.mechanism: A new Optional Parameter, Capabilities (type 2), carries a list of code, length and value triples, and a new NOTIFICATION Error Subcode 7 (Unsupported Capability) lets a speaker refuse a peer that lacks a capability.
tldr.outcome: RFC 2842 has been obsoleted by RFC 3392, which now defines the mechanism.

today: RFC 2842 is a Proposed Standard that has been obsoleted by RFC 3392, so that is the specification to read for BGP capabilities advertisement.

sections.title: How Capabilities Advertisement Works
sections.content:
A BGP speaker that supports the feature may include an Optional Parameter called Capabilities in its OPEN message. It lists what the speaker supports. A speaker learns what its peer supports by reading the list in the OPEN message it receives, and may use a capability only after it sees the peer support it.

If a speaker receives a NOTIFICATION with the Error Subcode Unsupported Optional Parameter in answer to an OPEN carrying Capabilities, the peer does not support capability advertisement. The speaker should then try to re-establish the connection without sending the Capabilities parameter.
sections.eli5: Each router shows a card of its skills. If the other router cannot read cards, the first one tries again without a card.

sections.title: The Capabilities Optional Parameter
sections.content:
This is Optional Parameter type 2. It holds one or more triples of Capability Code (1 octet), Capability Length (1 octet, the length of the value in octets) and Capability Value (variable, interpreted according to the code).

The same capability, identified by its code, may appear more than once in the parameter.
sections.eli5: Each skill on the card has a number, a length, and some details, like a label, a size and the contents.

sections.title: Refusing a Peer: Unsupported Capability
sections.content:
The RFC defines a new NOTIFICATION Error Subcode, Unsupported Capability, with value 7. Its Data field lists the capabilities that caused the speaker to send the message, each encoded as in the received OPEN message.

If a speaker supports a capability and finds its peer does not, it may send this NOTIFICATION and end the peering. The decision is local to the speaker, and such peering should not be re-established automatically.
sections.eli5: If a router really needs a skill the other lacks, it can politely say so and stop, and it will not keep redialing.

sections.title: Code Registry and Security
sections.content: IANA is expected to maintain a registry of Capability Codes. Value 0 is reserved. Values 1 through 63 are assigned by IETF Consensus, 64 through 127 by First Come First Served, and 128 through 255 are for Private Use, per RFC 2434. On security, the RFC says the extension does not change the underlying security issues of existing BGP.
sections.eli5: Skill numbers come in ranges: some need a big group to agree, some are first come first served, and some are private.
